title: The Pressed Mask

outcomes.completionNarration:
You put it on in front of her.

Vane does not flinch and does not look away either, which costs her something. She holds the lamp up and studies the muzzle-print where your own face should be. "Right," she says. "That is what it does." She writes two lines in the stair log and reads the second one out loud so you hear it as a fact and not a scolding: the mask is above the cloister, and a Collegian is wearing it.

"Keep it if you are keeping it. I would rather know who has it than wonder." She goes back to the wick. "Everyone who talks to you today is going to do that thing with their eyes. That is the cost. It was always the cost."

You carry it up unworn and set it on the step in the lamplight, which is all she asked for.

Vane turns it over twice with the wick shears rather than her paws. "Silk. Pressed round somebody and then left." She writes one line in the stair log and puts the mask on the high ledge, face down, where it can be seen from the stair. "I am not hiding it and I am not burning it. Somebody will want to know it exists."

Then she presses the flat tin into your paws. "Wick, taper, rag. A lit stair is worth more than a brave one, and you did the duller thing on purpose. Holm would have had opinions about you, and they would have been good ones."

introNarration:
Vane sets the shears down. "Two turns below the gallery there is a cloister with webs in the arches. On the floor there is a face." She lets that sit. "Not a body. A shell of silk pressed round a face and then left, hard as a nutshell and about as heavy. I have seen it from the arch and I have not gone in for it, and you may write that down anywhere you like."

She picks the shears back up. "Bring it up into lamplight. Carry it or wear it, that is yours to decide, but I want to be looking at it in good light either way. Then talk vane."
reminderNarration: "The cloister below the gallery. Bring it up to the stair and talk vane, or put it on first. Either way I want it in lamplight."
